methods.name: create
methods.summary: Upload your own certificate you want Cloudflare to use for edge-to-origin communication to override the shared certificate.
methods.description:
Upload your own certificate you want Cloudflare to use for edge-to-origin
communication to override the shared certificate. Please note that it is
important to keep only one certificate active. Also, make sure to enable
zone-level authenticated origin pulls by making a PUT call to settings endpoint
to see the uploaded certificate in use.

methods.name: list
methods.summary: Lists all client certificates configured for zone-level authenticated origin pulls.
methods.description:
Lists all client certificates configured for zone-level authenticated origin
pulls.

methods.name: delete
methods.summary: Removes a client certificate used for zone-level authenticated origin pulls.
methods.description: Removes a client certificate used for zone-level authenticated origin pulls.

methods.name: get
methods.summary: Retrieves details for a specific client certificate used in zone-level authenticated origin pulls.
methods.description:
Retrieves details for a specific client certificate used in zone-level
authenticated origin pulls.

methods.name: update
methods.summary: Associate a hostname to a certificate and enable, disable or invalidate the association.
methods.description:
Associate a hostname to a certificate and enable, disable or invalidate the
association. If disabled, client certificate will not be sent to the hostname
even if activated at the zone level. 100 maximum associations on a single
certificate are allowed. Note: Use a null value for parameter _enabled_ to
invalidate the association.

props.name: enabled
props.description:
Indicates whether hostname-level authenticated origin pulls is enabled. A null
value voids the association.

props.name: hostname
props.description:
The hostname on the origin for which the client certificate uploaded will be
used.

methods.name: get
methods.summary: Retrieves the client certificate authentication status for a specific hostname, showing whether authenticated origin pulls are enabled.
methods.description:
Retrieves the client certificate authentication status for a specific hostname,
showing whether authenticated origin pulls are enabled.

methods.name: create
methods.summary: Upload a certificate to be used for client authentication on a hostname.
methods.description:
Upload a certificate to be used for client authentication on a hostname. 10
hostname certificates per zone are allowed.

methods.name: list
methods.summary: Lists all client certificates configured for per-hostname authenticated origin pulls on the zone.
methods.description:
Lists all client certificates configured for per-hostname authenticated origin
pulls on the zone.

methods.name: delete
methods.summary: Removes a client certificate used for authenticated origin pulls on a specific hostname.
methods.description:
Removes a client certificate used for authenticated origin pulls on a specific
hostname. Note: Before deleting the certificate, you must first invalidate the
hostname for client authentication by sending a PUT request with `enabled` set
to null. After invalidating the association, the certificate can be safely
deleted.

methods.name: get
methods.summary: Get the certificate by ID to be used for client authentication on a hostname.
methods.description: Get the certificate by ID to be used for client authentication on a hostname.

methods.name: update
methods.summary: Enable or disable zone-level authenticated origin pulls.
methods.description:
Enable or disable zone-level authenticated origin pulls. 'enabled' should be set
true either before/after the certificate is uploaded to see the certificate in
use.

props.name: enabled
props.description: Indicates whether zone-level authenticated origin pulls is enabled.

methods.name: get
methods.summary: Get whether zone-level authenticated origin pulls is enabled or not.
methods.description:
Get whether zone-level authenticated origin pulls is enabled or not. It is false
by default.
